proposal: description-headroom: the two-way-boundary rule is running out of room against the 1024 spec cap
detail: 28 of 82 descriptions are at or over 1024 and 12 are within 60 chars of it. Every new talent must add a reciprocal NOT-clause to each contested neighbour, so each arrival spends headroom in K existing descriptions. The mechanism that keeps routing correct is consuming the budget that makes routing possible. This is now structural, not a backlog of sloppy descriptions.
options: A) Shorten clause FORM: name the neighbour without prose ('NOT: x, y'). Cheapest, buys maybe 40% per clause, does not change the growth rate.

B) Move NOT-clauses to the BODY. REJECTED ON MECHANISM, not on taste: the body is not loaded until the skill activates, so a body NOT-clause cannot prevent a wrong activation. It would look like a fix and silently do nothing -- the silent-defect shape.

C) Move them to when_to_use. REJECTED: verified 2026-08-28 that when_to_use is NOT in the agentskills.io spec, so this welds the library to Claude Code -- the exact trade DESCRIPTION_CAP_CHARS refused.

D) Treat the cap as a FORCING FUNCTION on library size: a talent that needs more than ~5 boundary clauses is evidence of a contested region that should be consolidated, not disambiguated further. Turns the wall into a consolidation trigger.
recommendation: D as the rule, with A as the immediate relief. D is the only option that addresses the growth rate rather than the symptom, and it converts a hard limit into the signal this library otherwise lacks: it has no prune trigger by design (disuse is never grounds), so it has nothing that pushes back on sprawl. The cap can be that. A buys room to apply D without an emergency.
gate: human -- routing-sensitive and architectural; changes what the library optimises for. Per CLAUDE.md this warrants an ADR, not a silent choice.

proposal: body-length budget: 81% of the library exceeds the 500-word budget writing-skills states, and writing-skills itself is 6.6x over it
detail: Measured over 84 skills: median body 910 words against a stated 500. 68 of 84 over budget, 38 over 2x, 13 over 4x, 3 over 6x. The longest are subagent-driven-development (4815), writing-skills (3306), expand-contract-migration (3144), doc-claim-reconciliation (2721). Unlike the description cap this is NOT a startup context tax -- bodies load only on activation -- so the cost is per-activation tokens plus the risk the tester named: a skill not read in full is a skill whose controls do not run, which is this library's own silent-defect shape one level up. The rule-stating file breaking its own rule by 6.6x is the same self-contradiction we found in three worked examples this wave.
options: A) Enforce 500 mechanically in preflight. REJECTED as stated: it would fail 81% of the library on day one and the budget itself is uncited -- writing-skills asserts it without a source.
B) Establish what the real budget should be (cite it or measure it), then set a cap and bring outliers down over waves.

C) Split long bodies into SKILL.md + supporting files, which the agentskills spec explicitly recommends ('Keep your main SKILL.md under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to separate files'). Progressive disclosure means a supporting file costs nothing until needed.
D) Accept the drift and delete the 500-word claim from writing-skills, so the library stops asserting a rule it does not keep.
recommendation: C, preceded by B. C is the only option the spec actually endorses and it cuts per-activation cost without losing content -- doc-claim-reconciliation's control table is the obvious first candidate. But do B first: enforcing or splitting toward an uncited 500 would repeat this session's cap error, where I acted on a number before checking where it came from. D is the honest fallback if B finds no basis for any number.
gate: human -- changes an authoring standard across 84 units, and the current standard is uncited
